kevin: Heads-up — after the kernel-affinity patch landed (yesterday), we see a regression in prefill-heavy workloads. p50 ~+6ms, p95 looks worse. Suspect batching interaction + KV churn.

maria: Any flamegraph/profile snippets? CI or prod?

kevin: Quick profile from a repro run (canary cluster):
```
# condensed perf dump
workload: mix-prefill-80pct
batcher: continuous (shared queue)
kernel_select: chosen=matmul_v2 fallback=matmul_v1
batch_formation: median=3, mean=4.2, tail=12
phase_mix: prefill_ratio=0.78
kv_cache: miss_rate=0.34, evictions/sec=180
latency_ms: p50=18.3 -> 24.6 (regression), p95=86 -> 140
```

joni: Interesting — kernel_select seems fine, but batch sizes are spiky. Looks like prefill requests are joining decode batches and causing long-tail kernels + KV cold-paths.

sam: I've seen this before — when prefill queues inline with decode, they prime large KV pages and evict hot entries used by subsequent decodes. That explains p95 spikes.

maria: So likely two orthogonal problems: (1) batch formation heuristic not phase-aware, (2) kernel fallback/affinity amplifies cost when mixed batches hit cold KV.

kevin: Agreed. Quick proposal: split the continuous batcher into phase-tagged lanes (prefill vs decode). Keep decode lane low-latency (min_batch_size=1, token_budget_target=6), prefill lane can be throughput-optimized (min_batch_size=4, token_budget_target=24). Also add a handshake window to avoid interleaving during batch handshake.

joni: Implementation notes: add PhaseTag to requests, update aggregator to prefer same-phase coalescing for X ms. We'll also add a KV-priming guard: if kv_evictions/sec > threshold, temporarily refuse prefill merging into decode lane.

sam: + add metric: `phase.batch_coalesced_ratio` and `kv.hot_evictions` so we can detect when separation helps. Also track kernel fallback rate per-phase.

kevin: Can we canary this? Suggested flags:
```
deploy batcher --env=canary --flag=phase_split=true --param=decode_token_budget=6 --param=prefill_token_budget=24 --param=phase_join_window_ms=8
```

infra-bot: Canary cluster deployed: batcher@canary v2.3.1-phase-split. Initial telemetry (10min): decode p50 down 2ms, decode p95 down 18%, overall prefill throughput +8%, kv_evictions down 41%.

maria: Nice. Any regressions on cold-start throughput?

kevin: Not visible in the 10m window, but need longer run. Also observed slight increase in resource fragmentation (more small kernels scheduled) — probable due to stricter kernel affinity when phases separate.

joni: Action items: (1) I'll land the phase-tag propagation + phase-heuristic in batcher (PR assigned), (2) Maria add unit + integration tests that simulate KV churn and assert decode p95 improves, (3) Kevin run 6h canary and capture kernel fallback rates.

sam: Also consider a soft-merge policy: if decode lane is idle for >X ms and prefill queue length >Y, allow controlled merge to avoid starvation. Config flags for operators.

kevin: Good idea. Let's keep default conservative. I'll file an experiment ticket with numbers and add the canary dashboard.

joni: PR posted: https://git.company/repo/prefill-decode-phase-split (WIP), contains feature-flag gating + metrics.

maria: Reviewed - left comments re: unit test determinism and a missing histogram label for `kernel.fallback.phase`.

kevin: Thanks. If everyone agrees, we'll promote to staging after 6h canary if kv_evictions and decode p95 improve. :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary 6h summary: decode p95 -21%, decode p50 -3ms, kv_evictions/sec -39%, kernel.fallback.rate per-decode -12%. No infra OOMs.

kevin: Excellent. I'll schedule staging rollout and update release notes with tuning flags and suggested defaults for heavy-prefill tenants.

maria: Note for docs team: add a short recommend config snippet for customers using mixed prefill/decode patterns.

joni: I'll follow up with perf bench numbers and a short postmortem if anything unexpected pops up.
